correctness.rationale: A cactus edge has precisely one alternative path; all other blocks join it at cut vertices and pass no current. Thus the outage resistance equals a sum of reciprocal conductances on the surviving cycle edges. The one-cycle cost in reciprocal conductances is strictly convex with affine detour inequalities and Slater feasibility. The unique threshold, explicit feasible resistances and multipliers satisfy all KKT conditions; cost is H²/d. Cycle expenditure bounds yield the sharp global S/B optimum, and equality forces unique per-cycle allocations. The sharp one-price threshold follows by solving the active-set equality. The included finite reproduction program passed 945 assertions, but is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Post-failure electrical resistance between the failed connection endpoints directly measures alternate-path quality in robust resistor or consensus-network planning. An exact optimizer across arbitrary real-valued edge prices on all bridgeless cacti determines every conductance, one sharp scalar price threshold per cycle, a global cycle budget division, uniqueness and a nontrivial equal-conductance price plateau. It is a natural complete structural result, not a recomputed table or an arbitrary numerical slice.
